title: Causal Signal Orchestration and Alert Decomposition Playbook
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines how Redwood teams orchestrate causal telemetry signals across the stack and decompose high-level alerts into actionable root-cause candidates. It establishes a standard signal taxonomy, a decision matrix for prioritizing signals, and a reproducible, semi-automated decomposition procedure to accelerate triage and reduce incident mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to repair (MTTR).

Scope: covers production inference services (hosted, dedicated, private), API gateways, runtime sidecars, and the telemetry ingestion/processing pipeline. Does not replace service-specific runbooks; it is a cross-service orchestration layer and playbook.

Goals
- Make alert surfaces more explainable by associating each alert to a ranked list of causal signal candidates (service, model variant, hardware, network, config).
- Provide a reproducible decomposition flow that is executable by an oncall engineer or by automation tooling.
- Ensure instrumentation is sufficient to produce causal hypotheses within 90s of an alert firing for 95% of alerts in the SLO-relevant corridors.
- Reduce noisy alerts by defining signal orchestration thresholds and adaptive sampling rules.

Definitions
- Causal Signal: a telemetry measurement (metric, trace span attribute, log fingerprint, synthetic check) that is a plausible contributor to a user-visible degradation.
- Decomposition: the structured process of mapping an alert to causal signals and then to a prioritized list of remediation or rollback actions.
- Orchestration Engine: the platform component (Alert Router + Correlator) that executes decomposition policies and surfaces candidates to the oncall UI.

High-level Architecture (text diagram)
- Ingress: API Gateway / Edge proxies generate request context and initial metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, token counts, request metadata)
- Runtime: model-serving runtime emits runtime metrics (kernel time, batch size, KV cache hit rate, quantization variant)
- Infra: GPU telemetry (util, temperature, EDC errors), network (RTT, packet loss), cloud infra events
- Telemetry pipeline: collector -> enrichment (context-bridge) -> correlator -> candidate scorer -> alert UI / runbook executor

Signal Taxonomy (canonical fields)
- request.context.source (client, tenant, route)
- runtime.model.variant_id
- runtime.kernel (name/version)
- runtime.kv_cache.hit_rate
- runtime.batch.size_distribution
- infra.gpu.utilization, infra.gpu.temperature
- infra.node.preemption_events
- network.peer_rtt, network.packet_loss
- policy.rate_limit.status, policy.fallback.invocations

Instrumentation Catalog (one-line table rows)
- Metric: runtime.kernel_ms (histogram) — ownership: eng-serving-runtime — SLI: 95th kernel latency
- Metric: kv_cache_hit_rate (gauge) — ownership: eng-serving-runtime — threshold: < 0.75
- Event: gpu_preemption (counter with labels node_id, signal) — ownership: eng-infra — used for immediate eviction correlation
- Trace: request-span (root + model-invoke spans with tags: variant_id, batch_id) — ownership: eng-developer-experience

Decision Matrix for Candidate Ranking
- Severity weight: impact on user visible SLO (0.5–1.5)
- Temporal proximity: signal co-occurrence within 120s of alert (multiplier 1.0–2.0)
- Cardinality: fraction of affected tenants/routes (multiplier 1.0–1.5)
- Signal fidelity: high (traces/metrics) vs low (logs) (multiplier 0.8–1.2)
- Historical recurrence: persistent vs transient (multiplier 0.9–1.3)
- Final score = base_score * product(multiplier) — candidates ranked desc.

Alert Decomposition Procedure (for oncall)
1) Acknowledge: Acknowledge the alert in the pager and open the Correlator UI.
2) Snapshot: Capture a 10-minute snapshot of key SLIs/metrics (request rate, latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token throughput, kv_cache_hit_rate, kernel_ms) for the affected route/tenant. Use the automated snapshot script: curl -s 'https://telemetry.internal/api/snapshot?alert_id=<id>' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' > /tmp/alert-<id>.json
3) Candidate list: Inspect the top 5 ranked candidates produced by the Orchestration Engine. If the engine did not surface candidates, run the manual correlation query (example below).
4) Hypothesis validate: For each top candidate, run targeted checks (see Check Matrix below). Mark hypothesis PASS/FAIL.
5) Remediate: Apply the approved remediation in order of candidate rank: a) config rollback, b) model-variant switch, c) capacity scale-up, d) circuit revert. Document actions in the incident page and attach the snapshot.
6) Post-incident: Add any missing instrumentation, tune thresholds, and create a regression test if the root cause was model or runtime change.

Check Matrix (targeted commands and expected indicators)
- Candidate: kv_cache_eviction_surge
  - Check: query kv_cache_hit_rate by batch_id and tenant for last 5m
  - Expected indicator for culprit: hit_rate drop > 20% coincident with latency p95 jump
- Candidate: kernel_slowdown_after-commit
  - Check: compare kernel_ms histograms before/after deploy tag
  - Indicator: new kernel version shows +40% p95 relative to baseline
- Candidate: gpu_preemption_spike
  - Check: infra events stream for "gpu_preemption" and pod restarts; validate with node-level EDC errors
  - Indicator: >3 preemptions in 2m for same node_id
- Candidate: network_tail
  - Check: peer_rtt and service-to-service span durations grouped by route
  - Indicator: 99th percentile RTT increase with no corresponding CPU/GPU util increase

Example manual correlation query (PromQL-style pseudocode)
- Correlate latency spikes with kernel latency and kv cache: 
  avg_over_time(request_latency_p95{route=~"/chat/.*",tenant=~"$TENANT"}[10m])
  / avg_over_time(runtime.kernel_ms_p95{kernel=~".*"}[10m])
- Use a join in the correlator to find co-occurring high kernel_ms and low kv_cache_hit_rate windows.

Automation and Playbook Hooks
- Automatic candidate enrichment: when an alert of category "latency-slo-breach" fires, the Orchestration Engine will:
  - attach the most recent 1m GPU events, runtime variant metrics, and last deploy tag
  - run fast checks (kv cache summary, kernel histogram diff) and produce a ranked candidate list within 45s
- Auto-remediation guardrails: Automatic scaling (scale up by 20% for up to 10 minutes) may be enabled for level-2 severity; any automatic rollback or model-variant switch requires a human approval step.

Runbook Snippets (examples)
- Swap to compatible model variant (CLI):
  rwinfctl model swap --tenant $TENANT --route /chat/standard --from variant-a --to variant-b --reason "latency-slo-breach auto-hold"
- Fetch quick snapshot (script):
  ./scripts/telemetry-snapshot.sh --alert-id $ALERT_ID --window 600 --out /tmp/snap.json

Ownership and SLAs
- Observability steward (eng-platform): owns orchestration engine policies and candidate scoring logic.
- Runtime team (eng-serving-runtime): owns kernel and KV cache metrics and guarantees instrumentation contracts.
- Infra SRE: owns GPU event telemetry and node-level signals.
- SLO for playbook efficacy: 95% of alerts in the latency/p99 corridor must have at least one valid candidate surfaced within 90s.

Rollout and Validation Checklist
- Phase 0: Unit test candidate scorer with historical incidents (five known incidents).
- Phase 1: Shadow mode for 2 weeks: surface candidates but do not show to oncall; measure precision and recall of candidate ranking.
- Phase 2: Soft enable for non-prod and non-critical tenants; request pager alerts to include candidate suggestions.
- Phase 3: Full enable with guardrails and limited auto-remediation options.

Compatibility and Migration Notes
- Telemetry enrichment requires consistent request.context propagation. Teams must adopt the request-context SDK (v2 or later) before the Orchestration Engine can fully correlate traces and metrics.
- If a service lacks kernel_ms or model.variant_id tagging, the Engine falls back to host-level signals with lower signal-fidelity multiplier. Add lightweight instrumentation adapters if needed.

Metrics to Measure Effectiveness
- Candidate precision@1 (fraction of incidents where top candidate matched final root cause) — target >= 0.65 in shadow mode.
- Time to candidate (median) — target <= 45s.
- Oncall acknowledged MTTA and MTTR relative improvement vs baseline.

Post-incident Actions and Governance
- Every incident where the playbook was used must include a short remediation artifact: missing instrumentation added, scoring rule adjusted, threshold tuned, or regression test created.
- Quarterly audit: Observability steward runs an audit comparing historical candidate precision and recommends policy changes.

References and Related Docs
- Telemetry ingestion and retention guidelines (observability-standards)
- SLO-driven runtime contracts and rollback playbook (eng-serving-runtime)
- Incident review template and postmortem guidance (oncall-and-incident-response)

Appendix: Common failure signatures and heuristic checks
- Signature: p95 latency up + request rate stable + kernel_ms p95 up -> likely runtime kernel regression or model variant quality degradation.
- Signature: p99 latency up + cpu/gpu util low + network RTT high -> network tail.
- Signature: error rate spike + deploy tag change -> suspect model or infra deploy; verify canary gating.
